## Overview

`essential8` computes Life's Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health scores using the American Heart Association's 2022 definitions. Subjects aged 20 years or older are scored using the adult definitions whereas subjects aged 4 months to 19 years are scored using the pediatric definitions; this vignette scores adults, see `vignette("pediatric-scoring")` for details about pediatric scoring.

This vignette shows how to score complete and incomplete data. The examples
use `dplyr` and the native pipe (`|>`, available in R 4.1+). See `?score_le8`
for all input requirements and scoring details.

## Create an adult data frame

Supply one row per person. This example includes two adults with responses
to the 16-item Mediterranean Eating Pattern for Americans (MEPA) questionnaire.
It shows both BMI profiles and both glucose measures.

```{r create-data}
library(essential8)
library(dplyr)

adult_data <- tibble(
  id = c("patient_1", "patient_2"),
  age = c(42, 61),
  sex = c("female", "male"),
  # Daily servings
  olive_oil = c(2, 1),
  green_leafy_vegetables = c(1, 0.5),
  other_vegetables = c(2, 1),
  whole_grains = c(2, 1),
  # Weekly servings
  berries = c(3, 1),
  other_fruit = c(5, 2),
  meat = c(2, 5),
  fish = c(3, 1),
  chicken = c(2, 4),
  cheese = c(1, 4),
  butter_cream = c(1, 5),
  beans = c(3, 1),
  sweets_and_pastries = c(1, 5),
  nuts = c(4, 1),
  fast_food = c(0, 2),
  alcohol = c(4, 0),
  moderate_activity_minutes = c(100, 60),
  vigorous_activity_minutes = c(25, 0),
  smoking_status = c("never", "former"),
  years_since_quit = c(0, 6),
  current_inhaled_nds = c(FALSE, FALSE),
  secondhand_smoke_home = c(FALSE, FALSE),
  sleep_hours = c(7.5, 6.5),
  bmi = c(24.2, 24.0),
  bmi_profile = c("general", "asian_pacific"),
  non_hdl_cholesterol = c(125, 145),
  lipid_lowering_treatment = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  diabetes = c(FALSE, FALSE),
  glucose_measure = c("fasting_glucose", "hba1c"),
  glucose_value = c(95, 6.0),
  systolic_bp = c(118, 132),
  diastolic_bp = c(76, 84),
  antihypertensive_treatment = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
```

## Compute LE8 scores

Pass the data frame to `score_le8()`. The returned data frame retains the
input columns and appends the derived activity measure, eight component
scores, the number of contributing components, composite score, a completeness
indicator, and cardiovascular health category.

```{r score-data}
scored <- adult_data |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "mepa")

scored |>
  select(id, mepa_total, diet_score, le8_composite_score, le8_category)
```

Each vigorous activity minute counts as two moderate activity minutes and is
recorded as `physical_activity_moderate_equivalent_minutes`. The
`le8_composite_score` is the mean of the eight component scores for complete
records. Categories are `"low"` below 50, `"moderate"` from 50 to less than
80, and `"high"` at 80 or higher.

The component scores are available for analysis and quality checks:

```{r component-scores}
scored |>
  select(id, ends_with("_score"), -le8_composite_score)
```

## Understanding the MEPA inputs

The MEPA response columns use the 16 screener-item labels shown above.
Use `mepa_columns` to map different column names to these labels.

- `olive_oil`, `green_leafy_vegetables`, `other_vegetables`, and
  `whole_grains` are servings per day.
- `berries`, `other_fruit`, `meat`, `fish`, `chicken`, `cheese`,
  `butter_cream`, `beans`, `sweets_and_pastries`, `nuts`, and `alcohol` are
  servings per week.
- `fast_food` is the number of times per week that meals are consumed from
  fast-food restaurants.

The screener defines `meat` as red meat, hamburger, bacon, or sausage;
`fish` includes fish, shellfish, or seafood; and `cheese` means full-fat or
regular cheese or cream cheese.

`score_le8()` evaluates each criterion and returns their sum as `mepa_total`
so that the derived diet input can be audited. The default MEPA sex field is
`sex`. If `sex` is absent, a field named `female` is recognized automatically; map any other name with, for example, `mepa_columns = c(sex = "reported_sex")`. Values are trimmed and matched case-insensitively as `"m"`/`"f"` or `"male"`/`"female"`. Numeric or character `0`/`1` values are also accepted, where `0` is male and `1` is female. A logical `female` column (`TRUE` for female) is also accepted.

## Choosing a diet scoring method

The `diet_method` argument defaults to `"mepa"`. If your data contains both MEPA and percentile inputs, split the rows into separate data frames and call `score_le8()` separately for each method.

`essential8` can also compute DASH/HEI-2015 percentiles if you collected data for those instruments. Use `diet_method = "dash"` or `"hei2015"` with raw food and nutrient inputs,the resulting data-frame is similar to the MEPA call. Otherwise supply the DASH/HEI-2015 scores to be converted to percentiles, or the percentiles themselves in the data-frame via `diet_value`. See
`vignette("population-diets", package = "essential8")` for the background,
scoring rules, and examples.

Here is an example where the percentiles are user-supplied:

```{r percentile}
adult_data |>
  mutate(diet_value = c(35, 95)) |>
  score_le8(diet_method = "percentile") |>
  select(id, diet_value, diet_score, le8_composite_score)
```

## Scoring tips

- For `diet_method = "mepa"`, `diet_value` must be absent or contain only
  missing values.
- For `diet_method = "percentile"`, MEPA columns are ignored. Supply
  `diet_value` as a DASH or HEI-2015 percentile from 0 to 100, calculated
  against the relevant reference population before calling `score_le8()`.
  If it is absent or missing, the diet component cannot be scored.
- Set `bmi_profile` to either `"general"` or `"asian_pacific"`. The function
  does not infer a BMI profile from race or ethnicity.
- Set `glucose_measure` to `"fasting_glucose"` for a value in mg/dL or
  `"hba1c"` for a percentage. Diagnosed diabetes requires HbA1c for scoring.

Three optional flags apply adjustments that require clinical judgment:
`apply_lean_muscular_bmi_override`, `apply_sleep_apnea_penalty`, and
`apply_prediabetes_metformin_penalty`. When these columns are absent, their
adjustments are not applied.

## Working with incomplete component data

Component inputs may be missing, their columns may be omitted, or optionally, you can choose to impute missing data using `score_le8(impute = TRUE)`. Supply values in the documented units. `age` must be complete and at least 20 for every row.

By default, `score_le8()` calculates the composite score when at least seven of the eight component scores are available. Choose any threshold from 1 through 8
with `min_components`. The composite is the mean of the available components
when the threshold is met.

```{r incomplete-data}
adult_data |>
  mutate(sleep_hours = c(NA_real_, 6.5)) |>
  score_le8(min_components = 7) |>
  select(id, le8_composite_score, n_components, le8_complete)
```

`n_components` reports how many components were scored. `le8_complete`
is `TRUE` when all eight are available. Missing values in individual rows
do not trigger warnings. If a component cannot be scored for anyone, a
warning names it. The warning also explains when too few components are
available to calculate any composite scores.

## Summarize, reshape, and plot scores

`score_le8()` returns its input with the extra class `essential8_scores`,
which adds methods for summarizing and plotting. `summary()` reports how many
rows were scored, the distribution of each score, and the categories:

```{r summary}
summary(scored)
```

`dplyr::summarise()` without any expressions returns the same
statistics as a data frame, one row per measure, optionally by group with
`.by`. Ordinary summaries, such as
`summarise(scored, mean_le8 = mean(le8_composite_score))`, work as usual.

```{r summarise}
summarise(scored)
```

`tidy()` reshapes the scores into long format, one row per person and
measure, ready for grouped analyses or custom plots:

```{r tidy}
tidy(scored, id_cols = "id")
```

`plot()` draws the mean scores with ggplot2. Use `type = "distribution"` for
box plots and `type = "composite"` for a histogram of the composite score by
category. The result is a ggplot object that you can modify further.

```{r plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), fig.alt = "Bar chart of the mean LE8 composite and component scores, with dashed lines at the moderate (50) and high (80) thresholds."}
plot(scored)
```

Row-wise verbs such as `filter()`, `mutate()`, and joins keep the class;
`group_by()` and saving to a file drop it. Use `as_le8_scores()` to restore
it, for example after reading saved scores back into R.

## Source-defined inputs

`score_le8()` returns an error when the AHA definition does not assign a
score. Examples include a BMI below 18.5, which requires clinical judgment;
a glucose value in the diabetes range with no recorded diabetes diagnosis;
and current use of both combustible tobacco and an inhaled nicotine-delivery
system. Review these records before scoring.
